recent_posts.title: 500 days building a Steam factory survival game from scratch without an engine
recent_posts.summary: A solo developer chronicles 500 days of building Terra Factor, a factory-automation survival game released on Steam, entirely from scratch without a game engine. Starting as a simple 2-week Stardew Valley clone, the project evolved into a multi-age open-world survival crafting game featuring conveyor belt automation, an infinite procedurally generated wasteland, a day/night cycle with enemies, and a unique 'spatial tesseract' mechanic that lets players nest factories inside cubes to manage complexity. The devlog covers the full journey from a basic window renderer to a feature-complete Steam release including tech trees, boss fights, and an alchemy system.

recent_posts.title: Terraactto indie game devlog with new biome and tesseract mechanic
recent_posts.summary: A solo indie developer showcases their survival crafting game Terraactto, described as a blend of Terraria and Factorio. The video covers a new biome featuring spatial compression mechanics via a composable 'tesseract' block that lets players build mega-factories inside a single block. Other updates include new cobalt-tier tools, a merator for efficient iron processing, growth accelerators, and early work on base defense via automated Arc Pylons. The game is currently in a demo on Steam with a beta 'Frontier branch', and early access is tentatively planned for the following month with a focus on polish rather than new content.

recent_posts.title: My 3 year journey learning game design and development
recent_posts.summary: A game developer shares their 3-year journey learning game design, from early itch.io demos to Steam releases. After struggling to create something they were proud of, they've finally developed Terra Factor, a game they consider genuinely fun. The developer reflects on the challenges of game design and invites others to wishlist their project on Steam.

recent_posts.title: Use this to improve your gameplay VFX when low-level programming
Complete system for making games without engines using Odin
recent_posts.summary: A game developer shares their complete system for creating games without traditional engines, built over 5 years of experience. The approach centers on three main systems: a simple 2D sprite renderer for graphics, FMOD integration for sound design, and a flexible entity system using a single megastruct. The developer provides a free blueprint repository and emphasizes rapid iteration, low friction workflows, and solving actual problems rather than imaginary ones. The system prioritizes gameplay programming ease over premature optimization, allowing developers to focus on content creation rather than engine architecture.

recent_posts.title: Switching to second channel for future streams
recent_posts.summary: The streamer announced that they will no longer be streaming on their main channel and will instead switch to a second channel. Subscribers are encouraged to follow the new channel and turn on notifications to stay updated on future streams.

recent_posts.title: Programming a lighting system for my survival game
recent_posts.summary: The developer describes their process of adding a lighting system to a survival game, covering initial attempts, challenges faced, and the final implementation. They discuss adjusting lighting values, using shaders, and incorporating torches to achieve the desired effects. There is also mention of using JavaScript and planning for future enhancements to the game.

recent_posts.title: I made this game in 30 days
recent_posts.summary: The post describes the author’s experience of developing a game in 30 days, detailing the challenges and progress made. The game involves collecting and selling resources, expanding land, and defending the base at night. It is compared to a mix of Fara and Factoria. The demo is currently playable online, and the author plans to sell the game in early access to fund further development.

recent_posts.title: conveyor belt o'clock
recent_posts.summary: A developer discusses their morning routine, struggles with backing up data, and the importance of committing code to a repository. They express a desire to set up a better storage solution for their large data needs and consider using a NAS. The post also includes discussions about game development, specifically troubleshooting and improving various game features, and details about setting up an inventory system for better UX.
